summary: Burst of 5xx errors from retry amplification during ingress shutdown causing upstream runtime watchdog restarts
description:
Issue summary:
Customers observed a rapid elevation in 5xx responses (mostly 502/503) on the chat/generate endpoint between 08:12-08:28 UTC. The initial spike correlated with an ingress node rolling restart. Client SDKs retried aggressively and the amplified inflight connections overloaded upstream runtimes, which triggered runtime watchdog restarts and a transient GPU eviction pattern. Impact: several high-traffic tenants on Dedicated saw 30-60s failures and elevated tail latency.

Impact:
- NimbusDocs (dedicated tenant) experienced request failures for ~16 minutes, affecting production availability for their chat feature.
- Platform-level elevated 5xx floor and increased runtime restarts across 6 pods in us-east.

Environment:
- prod cluster in us-east-1; dedicated GPU pool (A100-style).
- Affected service: api-gateway -> ingress proxy -> serving-runtime (runtime v1.9.2).
timeline: 2026-03-13 08:12 UTC - First customer report from NimbusDocs via support@; symptoms: 502s on /v1/generate and streams dropping
2026-03-13 08:13 UTC - Support triage: created ticket, notified SRE via #infra-support. Assigned Diego.
2026-03-13 08:14 UTC - Observed ingress rolling restart in us-east (k8s node upgrade). Connection drain started.
2026-03-13 08:15-08:18 UTC - API gateway metrics: accept_queue_growth + retry count spike (SDK retries observed).
2026-03-13 08:18 UTC - Serving runtime processes (6 pods) reported watchdog_kill and subsequent restarts, GPU driver nvml resets on two hosts.
2026-03-13 08:28 UTC - Retry storm subsided after ingress finishes rolling and ingress config tweaked to increase graceful drain to 30s.
2026-03-13 08:40 UTC - Support pushed customer-facing update, SRE continues post-incident analysis.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate an ingress node rolling restart while a high concurrency tenant is active.
2) Use Redwood client SDK default retry policy (rapid 3 retries) and send concurrent long-polling streaming requests and short generation requests.
3) Observe accept queue length growth on api-gateway and rapid inflight connection churn
4) Check serving-runtime logs for watchdog_kill and GPU driver reset events.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Short drain timeout on ingress combined with aggressive client-side retries caused a connection pile-up at api-gateway, amplifying load and causing runtime watchdogs to trigger restarts.
Hypothesis 2: Runtime memory fragmentation increased due to concurrent long-lived streaming sessions while GPU driver resets occurred on hosts, leading to GNMT OOM path and crashes.
Metric checks: confirmed 5xx rate correlated with accept_queue depth and SDK retry count. Serving-runtime CPU and memory CPC increased prior to restarts.
Correlation: two GPU hosts reported nvml resets within 30s of ingress restarts; those hosts hosted affected runtime pods.
actions_taken: 08:20 UTC - SRE increased ingress graceful drain from 10s -> 30s for rolling restarts to reduce connection churn.
08:22 UTC - Temporarily tightened api-gateway per-tenant concurrent connection soft limits for NimbusDocs to avoid wider fanout.
08:25 UTC - Set client-side suggestion: Support sent recommended retry headers (Retry-After) and a customer note advising to reduce SDK retry aggressiveness until platform config stabilized.
08:35 UTC - Identified two GPU hosts with nvml resets and cordoned them; migrated pods off of the hosts and restarted the runtime pods cleanly.
08:47 UTC - SRE deployed a throttling rule at the ingress to backpressure retries originating from the common SDK user-agent while preserving in-flight streams.
resolution: Mitigation: Increased ingress drain timeout and applied temporary throttle on aggressive SDK retry user-agents. Replaced two affected GPU hosts and restarted runtimes; 5xx rates returned to baseline by 08:46 UTC. Root cause: replay amplification from client retry patterns interacting with short ingress drain window, which amplified transient accept-queue pressure and pushed serving-runtimes past watchdog thresholds. Permanent fix plan: adjust default SDK retry policy in docs, add server-side short-window backpressure and a gracebackoff layer in api-gateway, and improve GPU host watchdog heuristics to prefer graceful eviction over immediate kill when nvml reset detected.
next_steps: 1) Engineering: Implement server-side rate-limiter that recognizes aggressive SDK user-agent patterns and returns 429 with Retry-After during ingress drain (owner: Diego).
2) Client SDK team: Propose and release updated SDK with exponential backoff baseline and jitter (owner: Priya Shah).
3) Infra: Add nvml-reset-aware eviction strategy to the runtime watchdog to avoid simultaneous pod restarts on the same host (owner: SRE team).
4) CS: Follow up with NimbusDocs with RCA and recommended SDK config (owner: Aisha).
5) Postmortem: Draft Confluence postmortem and rollout plan for a hardened ingress drain policy (target: 2026-03-20).
